title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.

providers.name: Salesforce (core platform)
providers.scope_notes: API availability depends on edition. Creation of Connected Apps is restricted from Spring ’26; assess External Client Apps for new integrations.

controls.name: Permitted Users: Admin approved users are pre-authorized
controls.what: Only users whose profile or permission set is assigned to the connected app can use it; others are refused.
controls.setting: Setup > Connected Apps > Manage > Edit Policies > Permitted Users; Metadata ConnectedAppOauthPolicy isAdminApproved (ECA: permittedUsersPolicyType=AdminApprovedPreAuthorized)
controls.quote: If set to true , only users with the appropriate profile or permission set can access the app. These users don’t have to approve the app before they can access it.

controls.name: API Access Control (Allow only admin-approved apps)
controls.what: Org-wide: only connected apps installed or approved by an admin can call the Salesforce API; a separate switch covers customer/partner users.
controls.setting: Metadata ConnectedAppSettings enableAdminApprovedAppsOnly / enableAdminApprovedAppsOnlyForExternalUser; Setup > Connected Apps OAuth Usage (install/unblock)
controls.plan: Must be enabled by Salesforce Customer Support
controls.quote: If true , only apps that have been approved or installed by the admin can call the Salesforce API. To access this field, you must contact Salesforce Customer Support to enable API Access Control.

controls.name: IP Relaxation
controls.what: Enforce (default) applies org and profile IP restrictions to the app; Bypass options relax them, and Enforce_RelaxRefresh skips them for refresh-token exchanges.
controls.setting: Connected app / external client app OAuth policies > IP Relaxation; Metadata ipRelaxation (ECA ipRelaxationPolicyType)
controls.quote: ENFORCE (default)—Enforces the IP restrictions configured for the org, such as the IP ranges assigned to a user profile.

controls.name: Profile Login IP Ranges
controls.what: Restricts the IP ranges from which users of a profile, including API integration users, can log in.
controls.setting: Setup > Profiles > [profile] > Login IP Ranges; Metadata Profile.loginIpRanges
controls.quote: The list of IP address ranges from which users with a particular profile can log in.

controls.name: Enforce login IP ranges on every request
controls.what: Checks profile Login IP Ranges on every request, including from client apps, not only at login.
controls.setting: Setup > Session Settings; Metadata SecuritySettings/SessionSettings enforceIpRangesEveryRequest
controls.quote: If true , the IP addresses in Login IP Ranges are enforced when a user accesses Salesforce (on every page request), including access from a client app.

controls.name: Lock sessions to the IP address from which they originated
controls.what: Binds a session to the IP it was created from.
controls.setting: Setup > Session Settings; Metadata SessionSettings lockSessionsToIp
controls.quote: Indicates whether user sessions are locked to the IP address from which the user logged in ( true ) or not ( false ).

controls.name: Refresh Token Policy
controls.what: Sets refresh tokens to valid until revoked (default), immediately expire, expire after a fixed time, or expire after inactivity.
controls.setting: Connected app / ECA OAuth policies > Refresh Token Policy; Metadata refreshTokenPolicy (ECA refreshTokenPolicyType)
controls.quote: infinite —The refresh token is used indefinitely, unless revoked by the user or Salesforce admin. Default setting.

controls.name: Connected app session timeout
controls.what: Sets how long an access token session from the app lasts; falls back to profile then org session timeout.
controls.setting: Connected app policies > Session Policies > Timeout Value; Metadata ConnectedAppSessionPolicy sessionTimeout
controls.quote: If you don’t set a value, Salesforce uses the timeout value in the connected app user’s profile.

controls.name: High assurance session required (Block / Raise session level)
controls.what: Requires MFA-level sessions for the app; flows without a user approval step, such as JWT bearer, are blocked.
controls.setting: Connected app policies > Session Policies > High assurance session required; Metadata sessionLevel/policyAction
controls.quote: For flows without a user approval step, API logins with the High Assurance session security level are blocked.

controls.name: Connected app creation restricted (Spring '26)
controls.what: New connected apps cannot be created without contacting Support; existing apps keep working and external client apps are recommended.
controls.setting: Platform default; contact Salesforce Support to re-enable
controls.quote: Connected apps creation is restricted as of Spring ‘26. You can use existing connected apps during and after Spring ‘26.

authentication.summary: OAuth bearer: authorization code, client credentials, JWT bearer and SAML bearer/assertion flows. External Client Apps or existing Connected Apps.

federation.details: An IdP-issued SAML assertion (org SAML SSO config) can be exchanged for an API access token. Note: the separate 'SAML bearer assertion' flow uses an app-signed assertion (app private key) and is not external federation.

ip_restriction.boundary: Profile login ranges and app IP policies; continuous per-request IP enforcement is separately configured. JWT/SAML bearer flows enforce IP restrictions.

lifetime.summary: Session timeout (inactivity); default 2 h; set per app, profile or org

renewal.summary: No refresh token; the client presents a new IdP-issued SAML assertion to get a new token. Continued access follows the IdP's assertion issuance.

administration.summary: Pre-authorize users, restrict OAuth scopes, apply permission sets/profiles, configure session/refresh policies, revoke grants and disable flows.
administration.conditions: API availability depends on edition. Creation of Connected Apps is restricted from Spring ’26; assess External Client Apps for new integrations.

sso.details: Issuance needs a SAML assertion validated against the org's SAML SSO configuration, but Salesforce login flows are not invoked.

offboard.details: Opaque tokens stop on deactivation; JWT-based access tokens stay valid until timeout.

inventory.details: Connected Apps OAuth Usage lists app sessions; docs do not say SAML assertion flow grants (which can run without a connected app) appear there.

inventory.ui: Setup > Quick Find 'OAuth' > Connected Apps OAuth Usage (click user count for per-user tokens)
inventory.api: GET /apps/oauth/usage/{appId}/users (Connect REST resource; external client apps)

sso.ui: Setup > Quick Find 'Single Sign-On Settings' > Edit > SAML Enabled (configure the IdP whose assertions are accepted)

usage.ui: Setup > Quick Find 'Login History' > Login History (filter/download; Application column)
usage.api: SOQL: SELECT ... FROM LoginHistory WHERE Application = '<app>' (LoginSubType for flow); ApiEvent WHERE ConnectedAppId = '<id>' (Shield/Event Monitoring); OauthToken.UseCount

reads.api: SOQL: SELECT Query, QueriedEntities, RowsProcessed FROM ApiEvent WHERE ConnectedAppId = '<id>' (needs Shield or Event Monitoring + View Real-Time Event Monitoring Data)

offboard.ui: Setup > Quick Find 'Users' > Users > Edit > deselect Active > Save

token_format.notes: Client posts a SAML assertion to the token endpoint; Salesforce returns its own bearer token.

log_sources.name: LoginHistory
log_sources.notes: Every OAuth token grant shows as a login with LoginType/LoginSubType, SourceIp, Application. 6 months; no add-on needed.

log_sources.name: LoginEvent / ApiEvent (Real-Time Event Monitoring)
log_sources.notes: Needs Shield or Event Monitoring add-on. LoginKey ties a session's events; ApiEvent has ConnectedAppId.

log_sources.name: OauthToken object
log_sources.notes: Current tokens per user+app with UseCount and LastUsedDate.

log_sources.name: SetupAuditTrail
log_sources.notes: Connected app / external client app config changes; at least 180 days.

credential_id_fields.notes: Connected app name used to log in
External client app ID; null if session already active
Ties all events in one session
SAML/auth provider config used (SamlSsoConfig or AuthProvider)

anomaly_cues: Logins via a SAML config (AuthenticationServiceId) that was recently added or edited
SAML-based token grants for admins from unusual SourceIp
Assertion-based logins outside IdP sign-in times (compare with IdP logs)

containment.steps: Disable or fix the SAML/IdP configuration or rotate its certificate; revoke tokens via /services/oauth2/revoke; delete AuthSession rows; freeze affected users.
containment.notes: Issued tokens remain until revoked or sessions deleted.

sample_query.query: SELECT UserId, LoginTime, SourceIp, Application, LoginType, LoginSubType, AuthenticationServiceId FROM LoginHistory WHERE AuthenticationServiceId = '0LE000000000001AAA' AND LoginTime = LAST_N_DAYS:7
sample_query.purpose: All logins that used one SAML configuration
